caption: Teva Branded Pharmaceutical Products R&D, Inc. v. Amneal Pharmaceuticals of New York, LLC
citation_line: Teva Branded Pharmaceutical Products R&D, Inc. v. Amneal Pharmaceuticals of New York, LLC, No. 2:23-cv-20964; aff’d, No. 2024-1936 (Fed. Cir. Dec. 20, 2024)
headnote_district_ruling: Judge Chesler ordered Teva to delist inhaler-device patents from the FDA’s Orange Book because the patents did not claim the active ingredient at issue, albuterol sulfate.
qualification_rationale: The decision addressed the boundary between drug and device patents in the Hatch-Waxman system, with direct consequences for the timing of generic competition and the availability of the statutory counterclaim remedy.
appellate_posture_note: The Federal Circuit lifted its stay and affirmed the delisting order in a precedential opinion.
decision_selection_note: Opinion and order of 10 June 2024 denying Teva's motion to dismiss the counterclaims and granting partial judgment on the pleadings — the delisting ruling. The docket text truncates before the operative half. Affirmed, No. 24-1936 (Fed. Cir. Dec. 20, 2024).
